content: 1. Bray N, Noyes J, Edwards RT, and Harris N conducted a mixed-method systematic review and developed a conceptual framework focusing on wheelchair interventions, services, and provision for children with disabilities. This study was published in BMC Health Services Research in 2014 (Volume 14, Article 309). 2. Graham F, Boland P, Grainger R, and Wallace S performed a scoping review on the use of telehealth for remote assessment of wheelchair and seating needs in both adults and children. Their findings were published in Disability & Rehabilitation in 2020 (Volume 42, Pages 3538–3548). 3. Graham F, Boland P, Wallace S, Taylor WJ, Jones B, Maggo J, and colleagues explored the social and technical readiness for a telehealth assessment service for adults with complex wheelchair and seating needs. Their study included a national survey of 79 stakeholders and was published in the New Zealand Journal of Physiotherapy in 2021 (Volume 49, Pages 31–39). 4. Salatino C, Andrich R, Converti RM, and Saruggia M conducted an observational study on the provision of powered wheelchairs in Italy. Their research was published in Assistive Technology in 2016 (Volume 28, Pages 41–52). 5. Gowran RJ, Clifford A, Gallagher A, McKee J, O’Regan B, and McKay EA examined wheelchair and seating assistive technology provision as a means to enhance freedom for users. Their study was published in Disability and Rehabilitation in 2022 (Volume 44, Pages 370–381). 6. Armstrong W, Reisinger KD, and Smith WK evaluated the CIR-Whirlwind wheelchair and its service provision in Afghanistan. Their findings were published in Disability & Rehabilitation in 2007 (Volume 29, Pages 935–948). 7. Toro ML, Eke C, and Pearlman J assessed the impact of the World Health Organization’s 8-step wheelchair service provision model on wheelchair users in resource-limited settings. This cohort study, conducted in Indonesia, was published in BMC Health Services Research in 2016 (Volume 16, Article 1186/s12913-016-1268-y). 8. Beaumont-White S and Ham RO explored whether powered wheelchairs enable or disable users. Their study was published in Prosthetics & Orthotics International in 1997 (Volume 21, Pages 62–73). 9. Post MWM, Van Asbeck FWA, Van Dijk AJ, and Schrijvers AJP investigated the availability of and satisfaction with services for individuals with spinal cord injuries. Their findings were published in Spinal Cord in 1997 (Volume 35, Pages 109–115). 10. D’Innocenzo ME, Pearlman JL, Garcia-Mendez Y, Vasquez-Gabela S, Zigler C, Rosen P, and colleagues conducted an exploratory study on the outcomes of wheelchair provision through two service models in Indonesia. Their research was published in PLOS ONE in 2021 (Volume 16, Article e0228428). 11. Visagie S, Mlambo T, Van der Veen J, Nhunzvi C, Tigere D, and Scheffler E studied the impact of structured wheelchair services on user satisfaction and functionality in Zimbabwe. Their findings were published in the African Journal of Disability in 2016 (Volume 5, Article 222). 12. Williams E, Hurwitz E, Obaga I, Onguti B, Rivera A, Sy TRL, and colleagues explored the perspectives of basic wheelchair users in Kenya and the Philippines on improving access to wheelchair services. This qualitative study was published in BMC International Health & Human Rights in 2017 (Volume 17, Article 22). 13. Suzuki KM and Lockette G conducted a client satisfaction survey of a wheelchair seating clinic. Their findings were published in Physical and Occupational Therapy in Geriatrics in 2000 (Volume 17, Pages 55–65). 14. Verza R, Lopes Carvalho ML, Battaglia MA, and Messmer Uccelli M demonstrated that an interdisciplinary approach to evaluating assistive technology needs reduces equipment abandonment. Their study was published in Multiple Sclerosis in 2006 (Volume 12, Pages 88–93).
